title: Functoriality of $\underline T$ in $T$
statement:
Let $\varphi\colon T\to T'$ be a continuous ring homomorphism of topological rings. For every profinite set $S$, the
maps

$$
\varphi_*\colon\underline T(S)=C(S,T)\to C(S,T')=\underline{T'}(S),\qquad a\mapsto\varphi\circ a,
$$

form a morphism of condensed rings $\varphi_*\colon\underline T\to\underline{T'}$
([def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]). Hence they also form a morphism of the
underlying ring objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]). This construction is strictly
functorial: $(\mathrm{id}_T)_*=\mathrm{id}$, and $(\psi\circ\varphi)_*=\psi_*\circ\varphi_*$
for every topological ring $T''$ and further continuous ring homomorphism $\psi\colon T'\to T''$.

proof.text: For each profinite set $S$ define $f_S(a)=\varphi\circ a$. This lies in $C(S,T')$ because $a$ and $\varphi$ are continuous. The rings of sections in [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] have pointwise operations. For every $s\in S$ one has $f_S(a+b)(s)=\varphi(a(s)+b(s))=\varphi(a(s))+\varphi(b(s))$, and $f_S(ab)(s)=\varphi(a(s)b(s))=\varphi(a(s))\varphi(b(s))$; also $f_S(0)=0$ and $f_S(1)=1$. Thus $f_S$ is a ring homomorphism, including when $S$ is empty.

For a continuous map $u:S'\to S$ of profinite sets and a section $a$, the restriction maps of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] give $f_{S'}(a\circ u)=\varphi\circ(a\circ u)=(\varphi\circ a)\circ u=f_S(a)\circ u$. Hence the $f_S$ form a natural transformation of presheaves of rings. Both presheaves are sheaves by the cited statement. A morphism of sheaves is a natural transformation between their underlying presheaves, so these components define the required morphism of condensed rings; there is no further descent condition for a morphism.

Part 3 of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] applies on the site of profinite sets to the sheaf-of-rings morphism just constructed. Its statement says that a morphism of sheaves of rings is a morphism of their underlying ring objects. Therefore the same underlying abelian-sheaf map is compatible with the multiplications and units in the item.

At every $S$ and every section $a$, postcomposition with $\mathrm{id}_T$ sends $a$ to $a$, and postcomposition with $\psi\circ\varphi$ sends $a$ to $\psi\circ(\varphi\circ a)$. Thus the component ring homomorphisms for identity and composition equal those of the identity and composite sheaf morphisms, respectively. Equality of natural transformations is equality of components, so $(\mathrm{id}_T)_*=\mathrm{id}$ and $(\psi\circ\varphi)_*=\psi_*\circ\varphi_*$. Forgetting to underlying abelian sheaves keeps these same maps, so the equalities also hold for their ring-object morphisms.
